'''Sarah Trone Garriott''' is an American politician and minister serving as a member of the [[Iowa Senate]] from the [[Iowa Senate, District 14|14th district]] since 2021. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], she represents part of [[Dallas County, Iowa|Dallas County]] in the [[Des Moines, Iowa|Des Moines]] area and served previously as Senate [[minority whip]]. She is the Democratic nominee in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa#District 3|2026]] election in [[Iowa]]'s [[Iowa's 3rd congressional district|3rd congressional district]].

== Early life and education ==
Garriott was born in [[Minneapolis]]. She earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in history from the [[College of St. Scholastica]], a Master of Theological Studies from the [[Harvard Divinity School]], and a Master of Divinity from the [[Lutheran School of Theology at Chicago]].<ref name="ballotpedia">{{Cite web|title=Sarah Garriott|url=https://ballotpedia.org/Sarah_Garriott|access-date=2021-05-07|website=Ballotpedia|language=en}}</ref> After earning her undergraduate degree, Garriott worked as a volunteer with [[AmeriCorps VISTA]] in [[New Mexico]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lifestory: US Pastor Rev Sarah Trone Garriott - Running for Office Is a Test of Faith|url=https://www.sightmagazine.com.au/columns/lifestory/14574-lifestory-us-pastor-rev-sarah-trone-garriott-running-for-office-is-a-test-of-faith|access-date=2021-05-07|website=Sight Magazine |date=22 January 2020 }}</ref>

== Ministry career ==
Garriott is ordained in the [[Evangelical Lutheran Church in America|Evangelical Lutheran Church in America (ELCA)]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=River |first=Brick |title=Sen. Rev. Sarah Trone Garriott Encourages Laity to Counteract Christian Nationalism |url=https://www.iaumc.org/newsdetail/sen-rev-sarah-throne-garrett-encourages-laity-to-confront-christian-nationalism-18119210 |access-date=2026-09-13 |website=www.iaumc.org |language=en}}</ref> In 2004 and 2005, Garriott was a chaplain at the [[Thomas Jefferson University Hospital]] in [[Philadelphia]]. From 2005 to 2008, she was a chaplain at [[Lurie Children's Hospital]] in [[Chicago]]. She later worked as a pastor at Lutheran churches in [[Bergton, Virginia]], and [[Clive, Iowa]]. Since 2017, Garriott works as the coordinator of interfaith engagement at the Des Moines Area Religious Council.<ref name="ballotpedia" />

== Iowa Senate ==

=== Elections ===
Garriott was elected to the [[Iowa Senate]] from the [[Iowa's 22nd Senate district|22nd district]] in November 2020, winning the open seat following the retirement of incumbent Republican [[Charles Schneider (politician)|Charles Schneider]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Republicans expand majority in Iowa Legislature|url=https://www.weareiowa.com/article/news/politics/elections/iowa-statehouse-elections-races-2020-live-results-legislature/524-c3eebf89-4087-4c57-81b5-54cf937fad4e|access-date=2021-05-07|website=We Are Iowa |date=3 November 2020 |language=en-US|last=McGee|first=Lakyn|last2=Knepper|first2=Hollie}}</ref> She defeated Clive mayor Scott Cirksena with 51.1% of the vote,<ref name=":1" /> after campaigning on expanding access to affordable health care.<ref>{{Cite web |last=LeBlanc |first=Sarah Kay |title=Election 2020: Trone Garriott leads in race for Iowa Senate District 22 |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/elections/2020/11/03/iowa-election-2020-scott-cirksena-faces-sarah-trone-garriott-senate-district-22/3742276001/ |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=The Des Moines Register |language=en-US|date=November 4, 2020}}</ref>

In 2022, following redistricting that paired her with another Democratic incumbent, Garriott chose to run in the newly drawn [[Iowa's 14th Senate district|14th district]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Richardson |first=Ian |date=December 1, 2021 |title=Democratic Sen. Sarah Trone Garriott will move districts, could face Republican Sen. Jake Chapman in 2022 |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2021/12/01/iowa-redistricting-democrat-sarah-trone-garriott-moving-dallas-county-face-republican-jake-chapman/8794928002/ |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=The Des Moines Register |language=en-US}}</ref> where she defeated the Iowa Senate president [[Jake Chapman (politician)|Jake Chapman]] by 51.5% to 48.5% of the vote<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sitter |first=Phillip |title=Trone Garriott defeats State Senate president Chapman in Dallas County |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/elections/2022/11/09/iowa-senate-presidents-race-among-those-in-dallas-county-too-close-to-call/69611710007/ |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=The Des Moines Register |language=en-US|date=November 9, 2022}}</ref> in the most expensive Iowa legislative race of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barreda |first=Virginia |title=13 Iowa races in the 2024 election we're watching |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/10/11/13-iowa-races-were-watching-in-the-2024-election-trump-harris/75570218007/ |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=The Des Moines Register |language=en-US|last2=Pfannenstiel|first2=Brianne|last3=Gruber-Miller|first3=Stephen|date=October 11, 2024}}</ref> She was reelected in 2024 after defeating Republican nominee Mark Hanson, a [[Dallas County, Iowa|Dallas County]] supervisor, by 29 votes following a recount, receiving 20,467 votes to Hanson's 20,438.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Payne |first=Marissa |title=Recount confirms it: Sarah Trone Garriott wins reelection to Iowa Senate District 14 |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/11/25/recount-sarah-trone-garriott-mark-hanson-reelection-iowa-senate-district-14-election-2024/76435532007/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=The Des Moines Register |language=en-US|date=November 25, 2024}}</ref>

=== Tenure ===
During the 90th [[Iowa General Assembly|General Assembly]], Garriott served as the senate minority whip.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Iowa Legislative Services Agency |title=State Senator |url=https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislators/legislator/legislatorAllYears?personID=30551 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251003045658/https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislators/legislator/legislatorAllYears?personID=30551 |archive-date=2025-10-03 |access-date=2026-07-07 |website=www.legis.iowa.gov |language=en}}</ref> In 2023, she introduced legislation to expand access to school-based mental health services through [[Medicaid]] by allowing students to receive services before receiving a formal diagnosis.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Nettingham |first=Shi-Quan |date=October 23, 2024 |title=Iowa Senator Democratic Incumbent Sarah Trone-Garriott Seeks Re-Election |url=https://www.raccoonvalleyradio.com/2024/10/23/iowa-senator-democratic-incumbent-sarah-trone-garriott-seeks-re-election/ |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=Raccoon Valley Radio - The One to Count On |language=en-US}}</ref> Following the [[2024 Perry High School shooting]], she renewed calls to increase mental health resources in Iowa schools.<ref name=":3" /> During Senate debate of House File 954 in 2025, she introduced an unsuccessful amendment that would have allowed local governments to conduct elections using [[Ranked-choice voting in the United States|ranked-choice voting]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Opsahl |first=Robin |date=2025-04-08 |title=Iowa Senate sends secretary of state's election bill to governor's desk • Iowa Capital Dispatch |url=https://iowacapitaldispatch.com/2025/04/07/iowa-senate-sends-secretary-of-states-election-bill-to-governors-desk/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Iowa Capital Dispatch |language=en-US}}</ref>

Garriott serves on the Education Committee and is [[ranking member]] of the Health and Human Services Committee.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Senator Sarah Trone Garriott|url=https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislators/legislator?ga=89&personID=30551|access-date=2021-05-07|website=legis.iowa.gov}}</ref> She previously served on the Commerce and Human Resources committees and the Health and Human Services Appropriations Subcommittee, and was ranking member of the Natural Resources and Environment Committee.<ref name=":0" />

== 2026 U.S. House of Representatives campaign ==
On May 5, 2025, Garriott announced her candidacy for [[United States House of Representatives]] in [[Iowa's 3rd congressional district]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-05 |title=State Sen. Sarah Trone Garriott launches campaign for US House seat, challenging Zach Nunn |url=https://www.kcci.com/article/iowa-third-district-house-election-candidates-zach-nunn-sarah-trone-garriott/64669613 |access-date=2025-05-05 |publisher=KCCI |language=en}}</ref> She ran uncontested in the Democratic primary, advancing to the November [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa#District 3|2026]] general election.<ref>{{cite web |title=Iowa House District 3 Primary Election Live Results 2026 - NBC News |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-primary-elections/iowa-us-house-district-3-results |publisher=NBC News |access-date=17 June 2026 |language=en |date=17 June 2026}}</ref>

During the general election campaign, she has emphasized health care issues, including restoring federal [[Medicaid]] funding and extending premium subsidies through the [[Affordable Care Act]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Opsahl |first=Robin |date=2026-07-07 |title=Trone Garriott calls for public option, restoring Medicaid funding at cancer event • Iowa Capital Dispatch |url=https://iowacapitaldispatch.com/2026/07/07/trone-garriott-calls-for-public-option-restoring-medicaid-funding-at-cancer-event/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=Iowa Capital Dispatch |language=en-US}}</ref> She also supported expanding access to health insurance through a [[public option]] and opposed cuts to federal cancer research funding.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Warren |first=Isabella |date=July 7, 2026 |title=Iowa House candidate Sarah Trone Garriott pushes Medicaid restoration, cancer research funding |url=https://www.kcrg.com/2026/07/07/iowa-house-candidate-sarah-trone-garriott-pushes-medicaid-restoration-cancer-research-funding/ |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=[[KCRG-TV]] (Channel 9) |publisher=ABC affiliate |language=en}}</ref>
== Personal life ==
Garriott is married to William Garriott, a professor at [[Drake University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=William Garriott {{!}} Drake University |url=https://www.drake.edu/lps/facultystaff/williamgarriott/ |access-date=2025-06-24 |publisher=Drake University |language=en}}</ref> They live in [[West Des Moines, Iowa|West Des Moines]] with their two sons.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Sarah Trone Garriott joins Faith Lutheran Church|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/local/clive/2014/01/07/sarah-trone-garriott-joins-faith-lutheran-church/4337729/|date= 2014-01-07|access-date=2021-05-07|website=Des Moines Register|language=en-US}}</ref>
